chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us with his own chain from Abdullah ibn Atta' al-Makki who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far: 'Your Shia in Iraq are numerous, and by Allah, there is no one like you among your family. Why do you not rise?' He said: 'O Abdullah ibn Atta', you have given your ears to the fools! By Allah, I am not your leader (al-Qa'im).' I said: 'Then who is our leader?' He said: 'Look for the one whose birth is hidden from the people, that is your leader. Indeed, no one from us who is pointed at with fingers and chewed upon by tongues will die except in anger or suddenly.'
ai.seo_question: Who is the expected Imam according to Imam al-Baqir (as) and what is the sign of his identity?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (as) corrects Abdullah ibn Atta's assumption that the current Imam would lead a visible political uprising, distinguishing the era of the Imams from the era of the Qa'im. He identifies the Mahdi as the one whose birth will be concealed (*ghaybat*), contrasting his unique occultation with the public visibility and sudden deaths of previous Imams who were 'pointed at by fingers.' This establishes the theological foundation for the Major Occultation, emphasizing that the true leader's identity will remain hidden from general scrutiny until his appointed time.
